b. 〈λαρόν:〉 sweet. Lg

459a. ἐψιόωνται: from ἐψία, which is jesting through words, as if it were some ἐπεσία from ἔπος; for this reason it is written with a smooth breathing. But when it has a rough breathing, it means 'they follow'.
b. 〈ἐψιόωνται:〉 they behave moderately in speech. Sm
c. ἄατος: the exceedingly harmful; for the first α is intensive, as in ἀχανές and ἀτενές. L
461. πορφυρέεσκεν: instead of 'he was pondering deeply'; for πορφύρα is a kind of fish found in the deep. Or instead of 'he was anxious about the danger both of land and of sea'.
462. 〈ὑποφρασθείς:〉 having observed. Lg

468. Ζεὺς τόσον: about the Cyclops Homer (ι 277): 'not even I, avoiding the wrath of Zeus, would spare you'. Through these words his arrogance is shown. And Homer also calls him impious (I 559): 'and he took up his bow against the lord'.

471. τοῖον μ’ Ἀρήνη〈θεν〉: Arene is a city of the Peloponnese; now it is called Erana, as Pisander says (16 fg 3 J.). He speaks arrogantly, as if 'you are not carrying me as a fellow-sailor, but as a helper'.
473. χαλίκρητον: the unmixed, that which relaxes the mind. The Athenians call unmixed wine χάλις. Aeschylus (fg 448 N.2) also says that the Bacchae are called χαλιμάδες.
475. Ἴδμων δὲ κα〈ί〉: appropriately he makes Idmon, being a seer, oppose Idas, who is an enemy of Apollo.
477. 〈ζωρόν:〉 the unmixed. Lg
478a. οἰδάνει: stirs up, raises, emboldens; the metaphor is from the sea, when it begins to swell.
b. 〈οἰδάνει:〉 persuades. Sm
481a. 〈ἐπιφλύειν:〉 to insult, to talk nonsense. Lg Sm
b. ἐπιφλύειν instead of φλυαρεῖν and λοιδορεῖν. P

482a. Ἀλωιάδας: Homer (Ε 385 sqq. λ 305 sqq.) also knows the story about them. Eratosthenes (241 fg 35 J.) says they were earth-born, and because they were reared by the wife of Aloeus, the myth arose that they were sons of Aloeus. Hesiod (fg 9 Rz.2) said they were sons of Aloeus and Iphimedeia by adoption, but in truth of Poseidon and Iphimedeia, and that the city Alos in Aetolia was founded by their father, which Homer (Β 682) mentions: 'who held Alos'.
b. 〈Ἀλωιάδας:〉 the sons of Aloeus. Sm
483. οὐδ’ ὅσον: not even a little. Lg (Sg) (P)
